I've been working this same land for decades. Quzhou is flat, the soil knows me and I know it. My 6 mu isn't much but it feeds the family and brings in a little income when prices are decent. Some of my grandchildren are in the city now, so sometimes it's mostly me and my wife managing. At 74, I can't do everything I used to, so I lean on the mechanical thresher and rotary tiller — saves my back.

For wheat this winter, I'll plant the same improved variety I've used for years — the county extension handed them out and the yields held up. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with urea in spring when the plants green up after cold. I water before the ground freezes, again at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain fill if it stays dry. That's four waterings — I've done it that way most years and it works. I'll spray herbicide once in autumn and a fungicide pass in spring against rust. Rotary till after maize harvest to get the ground ready quickly.

For summer maize, I buy hybrid seed from the village cooperative — Zhengdan or whatever they have that season, same as neighbors. I apply fertilizer in one go at planting — I know I should split it but it's harder to manage alone at my age. I'll water at emergence if June stays dry, then again around tasseling, and maybe once more in August. One herbicide spray early on. Rotary tillage right after wheat harvest to get the maize in fast — turnaround time matters here.

I'm not changing much from last year. What has worked for 55 years doesn't need fixing.
